title: Reject incorrect Southern South America source-to-Atlas crosswalk mappings

labels.name: status:ready
labels.description: Reviewed scope and dependencies ready for a worker claim

labels.name: type:geography
labels.description: Geographic source research, hierarchy/boundary evidence and proposals; no live mutations

body:
Raised October 6, 2026 (America/Los_Angeles), by post-merge Auditor `01a10892-0782-7b13-902c-d8b4db6c155d`. Affected [PR #922](https://github.com/ChengshuLi/WorldAtlas/pull/922), merge `d6a860ae2cff80af4ca0604bbc26e90dee56fc3b`, head `481a09861c33ada117ef4ffb02d36eff6b164d4c`.

**Executed finding:** the retained `verify-packet.py` reports `verification: passed` after changing the first Paraguay crosswalk row's `atlas_location_id` from `gb:PRY:ADM2:47425931B83994928044563` (25 De Diciembre) to `country-SPI` (Southern Patagonian Ice Field). The candidate CSV keeps 247 unique source IDs, 241 native rows and six aggregate-member rows. I also supplied a candidate packet index rehashed to this altered CSV. The original verifier checks crosswalk IDs/counts/types in aggregate, but never compares each row's actual target ID/name with the immutable baseline native/source-member mapping and does not validate the candidate packet index. It therefore falsely certifies an incorrect source-to-Atlas relationship. The committed crosswalk is correct against the retained baseline; this control demonstrates failure to detect candidate corruption, not an incorrect committed boundary dataset.

**Reproduce without mutating originals:** in an isolated read-only harness, execute the exact merged verifier while replacing only reads of `pry-source-crosswalk.csv` with an in-memory fixture containing that one changed target, and `packet-index.json` with a fixture whose CSV byte count/SHA-256 is updated. All other reads and nine Git baseline pins remain original. Its stdout still reports passed, 215 subjects, 32 parents and 247 Paraguay source records. A separately and consistently rehashed duplicate issue/scope fixture is rejected, so the failure is specifically crosswalk integrity. Inspection of `reproduce.py` also finds no row-to-derived-mapping target comparison, but its full execution is unavailable without the unretained 45,589,273-byte Paraguay original; do not claim that experiment was rerun.

**Expected behavior and success criteria:**
- In a separate new owned evidence vintage, establish exact source-ID→target/name/type relationships from the actual pinned baseline native IDs and aggregate member metadata, and explicitly label that as retained-baseline agreement rather than independent source geometry/legal verification.
- Validate every one of the 247 crosswalk rows, all 263 exact subjects (215 scoped units union 243 Paraguay crosswalk targets), the 215 unique unit rows and exact 32 parent/child inventories. Reject wrong or fabricated target IDs/names/types, duplicates, omissions and mixed scope/vintage rows even when fixture hashes are recomputed.
- Validate every declared packet file hash/size/inventory and reproduce or bind numerical results to actual checked rows. A successful byte/count check must not imply source-semantic validation. Missing oversized/unretained original inputs remain an explicit incomplete scope; do not synthesize their geometry or bypass 32 MiB/256 MiB limits.
- Run the original valid data plus meaningful adversarial controls and two deterministic runs; retain new immutable outputs/metric bindings and obtain substantive distinct exact-head review under the normal evidence/merge gates.
- Preserve all original #922 files, timestamps, source payloads, identities, geometry, hierarchy and historical results. Make additive evidence/validator changes only in the new owned directory; do not overwrite the original verifier/results or implement a core geographic correction.

Dependency #446 is closed/merged and its original implementation reservation must remain untouched. This issue is separate from #926–#930: those cover primary-source/legal/territorial research or engineering geography/semantics; this covers false-positive validation only. #1101 and #1107 concern different original packets/verifiers and exact subject scopes, so expanding their active scopes would be inappropriate. No production operation, import, deployment, geography approval or original-issue closure is authorized. Pins below refer to actual complete files at current ancestor main `27be77596f23304de6a720735538427e6d23e242`; resolve affected containing parts through the pinned world-index and describe them in the new manifest.


Auditor contract-format repair (2026-10-06): the current validator requires each named pin to be a SHA-256 string. These names bind the following actual complete files at `27be77596f23304de6a720735538427e6d23e242`; the new manifest must bind the same names to its `baseline.pin_files` descriptors. Scope, exact subjects, dependencies, mode and PR budget are preserved. Original evidence remains unchanged.
